cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: Oh hello. I wanted some information about the workshops in the school holidays.

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: I have two daughters who are interested.

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: The younger one's Lydia, she's four – do you take children as young as that?

cues.speaker: AH
cues.text: Yes, our Tiny Engineers workshop is for four to five-year-olds.

cues.speaker: AH
cues.text: For example, they work together to design a special cover that goes round an egg, so that

cues.speaker: AH
cues.text: when it's inside they can drop it from a height and it doesn't break.

cues.speaker: AH
cues.text: Well, sometimes it does break but that's part of the fun!

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: Right. And Lydia loves building things. Is there any opportunity for her to do that?

cues.speaker: AH
cues.text: Well, they have a competition to see who can make the highest tower.

cues.speaker: AH
cues.text: You'd be amazed how high they can go.

cues.speaker: AH
cues.text: But they're learning all the time as well as having fun.

cues.speaker: AH
cues.text: For example, one thing they do is to design and build a car that's attached to a balloon,

cues.speaker: AH
cues.text: and the force of the air in that actually powers the car and makes it move along.
